questions.q: How do I register to vote?
questions.a: Eligible Montanans may register to vote by completing a voter registration application (https://sosmt.gov/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?juwpfisadmin=false&action=wpfd&task=file.download&wpfd_category_id=46&wpfd_file_id=59393&token=&preview=1) and returning it to your county election administrator (https://sosmt.gov/elections/election-administrators-contact-list/). For more information, visit our Registration page (https://votemt.gov/voter-registration/)!

questions.q: How do I update my voter registration information?
questions.a: To update your voter registration information, including a name change, address change, or signature update, complete a voter registration application (https://sosmt.gov/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?juwpfisadmin=false&action=wpfd&task=file.download&wpfd_category_id=46&wpfd_file_id=59393&token=&preview=1) and return it to your county election administrator (https://sosmt.gov/elections/election-administrators-contact-list/). For more information, click here (https://votemt.gov/update/)!

questions.q: How do I cancel my voter registration?
questions.a: A voter may cancel their voter registration by submitting a signed written request for cancellation and the reason for cancellation to their county election administrator (https://sosmt.gov/elections/election-administrators-contact-list/).

questions.q: What are the deadlines for the close of regular registration for the federal primary and general elections?
questions.a: Regular registration closes 30 days before the election.

questions.q: What is late registration?
questions.a: Late registration is the 30-day period before an election. Eligible voters may register to vote or update their registration during the late registration period. In order to vote in the election, a voter must obtain their ballot in person. For more information, contact your county election administrator (https://sosmt.gov/elections/election-administrators-contact-list/).

questions.q: How do I get a new voter confirmation card?
questions.a: Voters may request a new voter confirmation card by contacting their county election administrator (https://sosmt.gov/elections/election-administrators-contact-list/).

questions.q: If I didn't vote in the Primary Election, can I vote in November's General Election?
questions.a: Yes. Not voting in the Primary Election does not disqualify an eligible elector from voting in the General Election.

questions.q: Where can I find polling place information and/or satellite location information?
questions.a: Yes. Your county elections office will designate polling places and other voter-specific information, which is available by clicking here (https://prodvoterportal.mt.gov/WhereToVote.aspx).

questions.q: When can I expect my absentee ballot?
questions.a: For a polling place primary or general election, absentee ballots will be mailed to registered voters on the absentee list 25 days prior to election day. You may track your ballot by clicking here (https://prodvoterportal.mt.gov/WhereToVote.aspx).

questions.q: What if I haven't received my absentee ballot?
questions.a: During the election, registered voters can track their absentee ballot online by clicking here (https://app.mt.gov/voterinfo/). If you haven't received your absentee ballot, please contact your county elections office (https://sosmt.gov/elections/election-administrators-contact-list/).

questions.q: Where can I find a sample ballot?
questions.a: Sample ballots are available during the federal primary and general elections. For more information, please click here (https://prodvoterportal.mt.gov/WhereToVote.aspx)!

questions.q: Where can I find information about school elections?
questions.a: Visit the Office of Public Instruction website at http://opi.mt.gov/Leadership/Finance-Grants/School-Finance/Elections.

questions.q: WHO IS ELIGIBLE TO VOTE ABSENTEE?
questions.a: In Montana, all registered voters are eligible to vote absentee.

questions.q: HOW DO I REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: You can download the form online (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/VoterInformation.htm), pick up an application at your local election office or the secretary of state’s office, or call either election office and ask to have an application mailed to you.

questions.q: WHAT IS THE DEADLINE TO REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a:
The deadline to request an absentee ballot (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/VoterInformation.htm) is the day before the election by noon. You can drop off your application in-person or mail it to the county election office with enough time before the election for processing and mailing the ballot to you.

A physical signature and your date of birth are required on the absentee application. If you plan to send the application to your local election office electronically, you should complete & print the online application, sign, scan, and email it attached as a PDF.

Once you have submitted your application, your absentee ballot will be mailed to you, or if closer to the election, given to you unless you indicate on the application that you have designated someone to pick it up for you

questions.q: WHEN ARE ABSENTEE BALLOTS MAILED OUT TO VOTERS WHO HAVE REQUESTED THEM?
questions.a: Absentee ballots for federal and state elections are mailed to eligible voters starting 25 days before Election Day.

questions.q: HOW DO I COMPLETE MY ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: After marking your absentee ballot, return it in the envelope provided. Be sure to sign the affirmation and provide your birth year on the return envelope before sending it back or dropping it off. Carefully read the instructions included with the packet.

questions.q: HOW DO I RETURN MY ABSENTEE BALLOT IN PERSON?
questions.a: Once you have marked your ballot, you can return it to your county election office  (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)before the polls close on Election Day in the secrecy envelope provided.

questions.q: CAN I TRACK MY ABSENTEE BALLOT?
questions.a: You can track your absentee ballot (https://prodvoterportal.mt.gov/WhereToVote.aspx) on the Secretary of State website.

questions.q: WHAT IF I REQUESTED A BALLOT BY MAIL BUT WANT TO VOTE IN PERSON?
questions.a: Most counties allow you to vote in person even if you requested an absentee ballot as long as you don’t submit your absentee ballot. Do not mail a ballot and vote in person. Please reach out to your local election office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more information.

questions.q: HOW DO I REQUEST AN ABSENTEE BALLOT AS AN OVERSEAS OR U.S. MILITARY VOTER?
questions.a:
Overseas citizens and U.S. military personnel can find information on how to register to vote and request a mail ballot from the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/overseas-voter-services)

Request Your Ballot Button (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/VoterInformation.htm?_ga=2.14087934.891015667.1714358523-1475019010.1654737627)

  Request your Ballot  (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/VoterInformation.htm)

questions.q: WHO CAN REGISTER TO VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
To register to vote in Montana, you must:

- Be a US citizen
- Be at least 18 years old on or before Election Day
- Have been a resident of Montana for at least 30 days before the election
- Provide a verifiable residential address or geographic information
- Not be convicted of a felony, serving a sentence in a penal institution
- Not be judged in a court of law to be of unsound mind

questions.q: WHO CAN VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
You can vote in Montana if you:

- Are a registered voter
- Are a US citizen
- Are at least 18 years old on or before the next election
- Have lived in Montana for at least 30 days
- Are not currently serving a felony conviction in a penal institution
- Have not been found by a court to be of unsound mind

questions.q: CAN I VOTE IN MONTANA IF I HAVE A FELONY CONVICTION?
questions.a: Yes, you can vote in Montana if you have a felony conviction, as long as you are not currently serving your sentence in a penal institution. Once released from incarceration, your right to vote is restored, even if you're on parole or probation. Pretrial detention, misdemeanors, probation, or parole do not restrict your voting rights.

questions.q: CAN I REGISTER AND VOTE IN MONTANA IF I DON’T HAVE A TRADITIONAL ADDRESS?
questions.a: Yes, you can register and vote in Montana without a traditional address. Citizens don't need a "permanent home" for voter registration. They can provide an alternative description of their residence, even if they are experiencing homelessness, as long as it enables the authorities to identify and assign them a voting precinct. This precinct assignment ensures that the voter receives the appropriate ballot. The mailing address on their registration form can be a P.O. box, local shelter, advocacy organization, outreach center, or the home of someone who will accept mail for them.

questions.q: AM I REQUIRED TO SHOW ID TO REGISTER TO VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a: Yes, you are required to provide identification when registering to vote in Montana. Your application must include one of the following: a Montana driver’s license number, a state ID number, or the last four digits of your Social Security Number. If you don’t have any of those, you must provide an acceptable form of ID.

questions.q: WHAT TYPES OF ID CAN I USE TO REGISTER TO VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
You can register to vote in Montana using:

- A Montana driver’s license or state ID card
- The last four digits of your Social Security Number

If you don’t have either of those, you may use:

- A military ID, tribal photo ID, U.S. passport, or Montana concealed carry permit
- Any other photo ID (e.g. a school ID) along with a document that shows your name and current address, such as a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government document

questions.q: WHAT IF I DON’T HAVE THE REQUIRED ID WHEN I REGISTER IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
If you don’t have a Montana driver’s license or Social Security Number, you can still register using alternative forms of identification. You must provide either:

- A valid photo ID (e.g. school ID, tribal ID)

and

- A document that includes your name and current address (e.g. utility bill, government check, bank statement)

If you fail to provide any acceptable ID, your registration will be considered incomplete, and you may need to present valid ID before voting.

Voters can call or text 844-338-8743 at any time to reach VoteRiders Voter ID Helpline

questions.q: What do I need to register to vote in Montana?
questions.a:
Here is what you need to know to register in Montana:

There are two methods of voter registration in Montana: register in-person or mail a printable application (https://sosmt.gov/elections/forms/#37-46-wpfd-for-montana-voters) to your county election office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: Can I register to vote using my college address in Montana?
questions.a: Yes, if you consider your campus address your residence, you can register to vote there. If you move to a different dorm or off campus, be sure to update your voter registration with your new address so you vote in the correct district.

questions.q: What’s the deadline to register to vote in Montana?
questions.a: Montana requires voters to register at least 30 days before the election if registering by mail. Online registration is not available, but you can register in person up to and including Election Day. Be sure to check the exact deadline each year.

questions.q: What form of ID do I need to vote in Montana?
questions.a: You must present a photo ID when voting in person in Montana. This can include a driver’s license, passport, student ID from a state-supported college, or other accepted forms.

questions.q: I’m originally from another state, can I still vote in my home state while studying in Montana?
questions.a: Yes, you can vote in your home state using an absentee ballot, but you'll need to follow your home state's rules and deadlines. You can find the rules for your state on VOTE411 or by contacting your state’s election office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm?_ga=2.80770708.201004602.1748545947-889989650.1701105430).

questions.q: Does registering to vote affect my financial aid, parents’ taxes, and/or tuition in Montana?
questions.a: Registering to vote in your college community will not affect your Federal Financial Aid, status as a dependent on your parents’ taxes, or tuition status.

questions.q: DO I NEED TO SHOW ID WHEN I VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a: Yes. Montana requires you to show a valid photo ID when voting in person. Election workers will ask for a physical copy of your ID that is current, valid, and readable.

questions.q: WHAT TYPES OF ID CAN I USE TO VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
You can use any one of the following valid photo IDs:

- Montana Driver’s License or REAL ID
- Montana State ID Card
- Military ID
- Tribal Photo ID
- US Passport
- Montana Concealed Carry Permit
- Montana University System or NAIA Photo ID

If you don’t have one of the IDs above, you may also:

- Bring a photo ID (any kind) plus one of the following documents that shows your name and current address:
- Utility bill
- Bank statement
- Paycheck or government check
- Government document

questions.q: WHAT IF I DON’T HAVE AN ACCEPTABLE ID WHEN I GO TO VOTE IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
If you do not have an acceptable form of ID, you should contact your county election official (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm?_ga=2.80770708.201004602.1748545947-889989650.1701105430) to learn about provisional voting options. You may still be able to vote, but you'll need to verify your identity later for your ballot to count. If you’re having trouble obtaining ID, you can also contact the Secretary of State’s office at [email protected] (https://www.vote411.org/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#fb8894889e979e988f92949588bb968fd59c948d) for assistance.

 Voters can call or text 844-338-8743 at any time to reach VoteRiders Voter ID Helpline

questions.q: HOW CAN I CHECK MY REGISTRATION STATUS?
questions.a: You can verify your voter registration status using Montana’s voter information tool (https://prodvoterportal.mt.gov/WhereToVote.aspx).

questions.q: WHO IS ELIGIBLE TO REGISTER IN MONTANA?
questions.a:
To register to vote in Montana, you must be:

- At least 18 years old on or before Election Day
- A U.S. citizen
- A resident of Montana and of the county in which you intend to vote for at least 30 days (you must provide an address to prove you live in the county)
- Not convicted of a felony, serving a sentence in a penal institution
- Not judged in a court of law to be of unsound mind

questions.q: HOW DO I UPDATE MY VOTER REGISTRATION?
questions.a: To update your voter registration information, including a name change, address change, or signature update, complete a voter registration application (https://www.vote411.org/register) and return it to your county election office (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: WHAT ADDRESS SHOULD I REGISTER AT IF I DON’T HAVE A RESIDENCE?
questions.a:
It is not mandatory for you to have a "permanent home" for voter registration. You can provide an alternative description of your residence, even if you are experiencing homelessness, as long as it enables the authorities to identify and assign a voting precinct to you. The mailing address on your registration form can be a PO box, local shelter, advocacy organization, outreach center, or the home of someone who will accept mail for you.

Not registered? Use our online registration tool (https://www.vote411.org/register) to complete your application!

questions.q: Ballot Notice and Cure Process
questions.a:
The deadline to cure (correct) your absentee/mail ballot is by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Election administrators will contact you via letter, phone, or email if any errors are found. The notice will include the necessary information and instructions to correct your ballot on time. You can also track your ballot through your state’s online tool (https://prodvoterportal.mt.gov/WhereToVote.aspx). If your ballot was rejected, you will likely need to submit a form called a "Ballot Rejection Notice" to your county elections office along with a copy of your ID by the deadline listed above.

If you voted a provisional ballot, you have until 5 p.m. on the day after the election to provide valid identification or eligibility information either in person, email, or postmarked.

questions.q: Campaign Finance Information
questions.a:
For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).

For information on state campaign contributions, please visit your state's resource (http://campaignreport.mt.gov/).

questions.q: Candidate and Ballot Measure Information
questions.a: Information on local, state and federal candidates and ballot measures may be available here (https://www.vote411.org/ballot#.UFoDEFHh-Sp).

questions.q: Drop Boxes
questions.a: You can hand-deliver your ballot to your county election office or drop it off at any polling location in your county on election day. You can find the location of your county election office here (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: Early Voting
questions.a:
Early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins on October 5th and ends on November 2nd.

In-person Absentee (Early Voting) Starts: 30 days before Election Day

In-person Absentee (Early Voting) Early Voting Ends: Noon the day before Election Day

Early voting takes place in the form of in-person absentee voting that allows voter, as soon as absentee ballots are available, to receive, mark and submit an absentee ballot in person at the election office or by mail to the election office.

However, ballots are not counted until election day. Early-in person absentee voting does not require a reason and starts as soon as ballots are available – by not later than 30 days before an election. For more information about times and locations please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: Election Dates
questions.a:
The next election dates can be found here https://www.vote411.org/montana.

Check your state's resource (https://sosmt.gov/elections/calendars/) for more information on local election dates and information.

questions.q: Election Day Voting Hours
questions.a: Poll hours of operation vary. Polling places open between 7:00 am and 12:00 pm and close at 8:00 pm. Contact your local elections official (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for exact times.

questions.q: Official Election Results
questions.a:
Official results are never available on Election Day. Election officials are working around the clock to count an unprecedented number of ballots, and it’s essential that they take the time to make sure every vote is counted.

Official election results will be uploaded on Montana’s Secretary of State website (https://sosmt.gov/elections/results/) as they become available.

  Official Results  (https://sosmt.gov/elections/results/)

questions.q: Overseas and Military Voters
questions.a:
You are a Military or Overseas voter if you are in uniformed services, living overseas OR a spouse or dependent of a uniformed services voter. To get registered and vote, you can utilize Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/about-contact)

If you have additional questions about elections and voting overseas you can use our state specific elections official directory or contact the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/about-contact)

questions.q: Poll Worker Information
questions.a:
You can make sure we have safe, fair, and efficient elections for all. Become a poll worker toda (https://powerthepolls.org/lwv )y!

In order to be a poll worker in Montana, you must:

- Be registered to vote in Montana
- Be at least 18 years of age
- Be a resident of the precinct
- Complete required training

To sign up, contact your local board of elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: Polling Place Locations
questions.a:
You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource (http://app.mt.gov/voterinfo/).

If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your county clerk (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/vote/election-official-directory). (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

questions.q: Primary Election Process
questions.a:
Montana is an “open primary” state. You can choose the party’s ballot you wish to vote. This decision does not register you with that party and it is a private decision.

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

questions.q: Provisional Voting
questions.a:
You may vote a provisional ballot if you meet specific conditions.

You will be asked to vote a provisional ballot for at least one of the following reasons:

- Your name is not in the precinct register
- The precinct register indications that you are provisionally registered, which has not been resolved
- You have claimed registration with Motor Vehicle Division or other agency, which could not be immediately confirmed
- You swore that you were eligible to vote due to not receiving or destroying your absentee ballot
- Your right to vote was challenged at the polls
- Your ID was insufficient and/or did not include a valid form of ID
- You failed to sign the register
- You are a late registrant who voted provisionally
- You show up to the polls to vote, but the register says you have an active absentee ballot

If necessary, you must provide clear and convincing evidence either on Election Day or by 5pm the day after the election in order to verify your identity and/or eligibility to have your provisional ballot counted. You may provide this information in person, by fax, by email or by mail postmarked by the day after election day.

Provisional Ballots are counted 6 days after the election.

questions.q: Provisions for Voters with Disabilities
questions.a:
If you have a physical disability or are unable to read or write, you may ask an election judge to help you mark your ballot for you. With the permission of the election judge, a friend or relative can go into the voting booth with you and help you vote.

Every polling place in Montana is required to have at least one specialized voting machine enabling people with disabilities to vote independently.If you would like to designate an agent to assist you with the voting process, contact your  local elections office (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/vote/election-official-directory)  (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)to ask for an application for the designation of an agent.

If you cannot enter your polling place, an election judge will assist you with curbside voting.

You may also apply for an electronic ballot that can be marked on your personal computer, printed and returned by mail or in person to the election office. Please check with your local elections office for more information.

For more information, you can utilize the American Association of People With Disabilities (AAPD) (http://www.aapd.com/what-we-do/voting/) resource or your states resource.  (https://sosmt.gov/elections/disabilities/)

questions.q: Time Off To Vote
questions.a: Time off to vote is subject to the employer, there is no requirement for employers to grant time off to vote for employees.

questions.a:
To verify your voter registration status

questions.q: Vote by Mail
questions.a:
Mail ballot elections do not involve the use of polling places since all qualified active and provisionally registered voters are mailed ballots on the same day without having to request them. Any municipal (city or town) election or district election (school, fire, water and sewer, etc.) can be conducted by mail ballot, if agreed to by the governing body.

Other options for returning a mail ballot:

You may still choose to vote in person in the election administrator’s office as soon as ballots are available. Or, you can make a signed written request that the ballot be mailed to an address other than the address that appears on your registration application if you will be away during a mail ballot election.

You also have the option to drop your ballot off at the county election office or, at other places of deposit noted in your mail ballot materials.

questions.q: Voting Machines
questions.a:
The voting systems used in Montana are optical scan and paper ballot.

Optical Scan: With this system, you will receive a card or sheet of paper, which you take over to a private table or booth. The card has the names of the various candidates and ballot measures printed on it. With a pen or pencil you fill in a little box or circle or the space between two arrows. When you are finished filling out all the cards, you may bring the cards over to a ballot box, where poll workers will show you how to put the cards in the box. Or in some places, you may feed the completed cards or papers into a computer device that checks your card or paper right there at the polling place to make sure you have voted the way you want to and counts the votes.

Paper Ballots: Paper ballots are one of the oldest ways of voting in America. They are still used in a few places on Election Day. When you come to the polling place, you will get a paper ballot from the poll worker. You take it to the voting booth, and use a pen or pencil to mark a box next to your candidate and issue choices. You then drop the marked ballot into a sealed ballot box.

You can learn more about voting systems by checking out the Elections Assistance Commission's (EAC) resource.  (https://www.eac.gov/testing_and_certification/voluntary_voting_system_guidelines.aspx)
